svg.title: Holomodel v3: where the hand-tracking chain was wrong, and what each fault cost
svg.desc: The same chain as docs/chain.svg — cameras and the LAN bridge into the solver, the solver into the shared input object, the input object into the grab, the grab onto the rig — with the twenty-one confirmed faults marked at the file and line they live in, each with the measured cost before the fix and the measured number after it. Every figure comes from a test in test/ that fails on v3-cams and passes on v3-cams-final.
svg.text: Holomodel v3 — the hand-tracking chain, and the 21 faults now fixed on v3-cams-final
Every red figure was measured against the code as it stood; every green one is the same measurement after the fix. Both come from tests in test/ that fail on v3-cams and pass here.
Priority order the numbers serve: 1) the rig shows the model correctly, 2) you can pick it up, move it and drop it. Nothing here is about Fable or sculpting.
1 · SENSORS AND CAPTURE
pixels and timestamps · public/js/input/
ZED 2i (side-by-side)
two eyes, one exposure → hands
cameras.js openSource · stereo.js
2 × Logitech 1080p
the head, for the off-axis projection
devices.js planRoles
ZED SDK over the LAN
3D hands from the CUDA laptop
zed-client.js
one plain webcam
today's app, the degradation target
webcam.js
BLOCKER · zed-client.js:151
hands that land before the first pong
was: stamped on the bridge's epoch clock →
a ghost hand holds the model for ever
now: unsynced = stamped on our clock, and every
staleness test is two-sided, so it expires
BUG · cameras.js:333 FrameGate
a worker that stops answering
was: 1 slot held for ever, 3606 busy drops in
60 s, both ZED eyes dead, fps still read 30
now: watchdog frees it, fps reads 0, 3 strikes
and the camera is given up so the ladder degrades
BUG · cameras.js:259 + stereo.js:55
which lens is this, really
was: three focal lengths for one ZED (514 / 518 /
700 px). A hand at 400 mm published at 989 mm
now: one measured figure, and the status line
says when the millimetres are still a guess
BUG · cameras.js:638 · webcam.js
was: Stop/Start leaked a camera stream and two
MediaPipe landmarkers, every time
now: stopCamera() gives all of it back
MINOR · cameras.js:605
was: 18 001 notes after 10 min of a dead graph,
0.9 MB re-joined into the DOM 60x a second
now: capped at 12, and the tracker is stopped
2 · THE SOLVER (geometry)
millimetres, rig frame · public/js/track/
line the cameras up in time
each camera samples at its own phase, so
every view is interpolated to one instant
solve.js CameraTrack.sampleAt / blend
match hands across cameras
handedness first, then reprojection error
solve.js matchHandsAcrossCameras
triangulate 21 landmarks
weighted per view, outliers voted out
triangulate.js · filter.js
or fall back to one camera
depth from palm size — about 10x worse
solve.js monoHandToRig
BLOCKER · solve.js:238 grouping
a missed detection is a RESULT, not silence:
the worker posts { face: null, hands: [] }
was: that empty frame hid the good frame 16 ms
earlier. 10% miss rate → 33% of frames on the
mono guess, fingertip 12.6 mm (p95 54 mm)
now: group on "has a usable frame in the stale
bound" → 0% mono, 2.7 mm (p95 5.3 mm)
BUG · solve.js:44 blend at t = 1
was: the reference camera blends with itself every
frame and the OLDER frame decided which hands
now: iterate the newer frame; blend(a,b,1) === b
BUG · solve.js:495 reject sentinel
was: 1e6 meant "not the same hand", but
Number.isFinite(1e6) is true → a 407 mm phantom
now: Infinity, plus a reprojection gate at 8 px
BUG · calibrate.js:221
was: a fingertip waved in one PLANE gave a pose
30-70 deg wrong with a healthy 1 px RMS
now: refused, with a reason the user can act on
stereo.js and calibrate.js now agree on the ZED's
stereo rotation — it was 5.7 mm of depth, one way
3 · SHARED INPUT AND THE GRAB
centimetres, app frame · interact/
input/state.js
eye, two hands, 21 joints, pinch, seenAt
the one contract the whole app reads
solve.js publish() → wire.js
pinch, with two thresholds
25 mm in, 30 mm out, plus a hold time
grab.js readHand
what did you mean to take
intent memory: what the OPEN hand was near
grab.js bestTarget / updateIntent
hold, carry, release, settle
anchored offset, deadband, spring, throw
grab.js driveHold / endHold
BLOCKER · config.js:59 default volume
was: a scene that did not state its own working
volume was clamped into the demo's metre box —
28 cm of travel on the first grab, 156 mm in one frame
now: no volume given → no clamp, no gravity, and a warning
BUG · grab.js:135 target ranking
was: ranked by (distance − bounding-SPHERE radius),
and the sphere was half the box DIAGONAL: a 30×2×30
cm base beat the ball on it, 30 times out of 30
now: distance to the part's own box, radius capped
BUG · grab.js:133 re-grab lockout
was: the lockout skipped the part you just dropped
and handed the grab to its NEIGHBOUR for 620 ms
now: the winner is locked out → take nothing
BUG · grab.js:295 losing tracking mid-carry
was: treated like a deliberate let-go — rolled back
24 mm and released at 45 cm/s, then fell 9 cm.
A camera blink was indistinguishable from a throw
now: 0.0 cm/s, 1.3 mm — it stays where it was
BUG · grab.js:247 two-hand blink
was: frozen for the gap, then 38 mm in one frame
now: 12.7 mm — inside an ordinary carrying frame
hold-through is one window again: 464 ms → 256 ms,
and a rotated part rests ON the floor, not 45 mm above it
4 · THE RIG
Pepper's ghost · view.js, sim/
portrait monitor, tilted, above
only a 4:3 area of it is used; the rest is
black, because black is what the acrylic
does not reflect
sim/rig-sim.js rigGeometry
head-tracked off-axis frustum
Kooima's generalised perspective, built
from input.eye every frame
view.js applyOffAxis
the virtual image
the panel mirrored in the sheet — where
the hands actually reach
parallax gain 0.20 on this rig
BLOCKER · solver.js:181 eye nudge
the rig's own eye-height calibration knob
was: re-added on EVERY frame that published
no eye. input.eye.y reached 120 cm after 1 s
and 1200 cm after 10 s — the frustum shears
off the panel and the rig shows black
now: applied inside publish(), once, or not at all
BUG · rig-sim.js — the simulator itself
was: it could not express a calibration error at
all (its one hook was overwritten), it modelled
a dropped frame as silence rather than as an
empty result, its ZED lens was 26% short, and
its two eyes were the wrong way round
now: all four fixed, so the millimetres it prints
are about the rig and not about its own model
what the simulator now says
planned kit, 1 px noise, 300 frames:
fingertip 2.5 mm mean, 4.4 mm p95
eye 1.9 mm mean, 3.5 mm p95
...assuming exact calibration. Under the
residual this project's own calibration
leaves (1.3% scale, 0.3°):
fingertip 16.1 mm
so: add the side view
the second webcam aimed at the hands
instead of the head holds 3.8 mm under
the same band, against 16.1 mm
px + t
mm
cm
